items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: No block contradicts its own sentence. Two figures on the page don't line up, though. Watch and Next say settling the pick takes 111,255 cases, but claim settle's table prints only 38,350 (one-sided) and 54,451 (two-sided), and nothing tells the reader that 111,255 is the two-sided, four-in-five size. Claim price's caption says neither step's gain carries an interval, while claim multihop prints an unpaired interval of -0.4 to +2.1 on that same pick-to-fallback gain.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The pick's thin margin is shown clearly in the headline, claim thin and claim settle. But the confidence reads High over a caveat its own figures make material: the pick's interval of 96.2–98.1% crosses the gate, and a fresh run reads it below 38.6% of the time. Claim multihop says multi-hop is where high reasoning 'gains most' (+1.7), but the task rows have no interval and the overall gain's interval crosses zero.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted bears on the call. Calls per task, effects outside Brisk-S and retry-by-model differences don't touch the gate or cost order among passing options, and per-task figures stay in the appendix.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Claim multihop's own figure, the pick's 95.6% on multi-hop, is not in its block, which draws only differences. Claim price's block leaves out the gains it divides by (+0.8 and +0.7 points). Claim retry's $0.014 cost is not drawn, and one of its bounds prints as '+0.03535'. Claims pick, thin and settle are well matched to their blocks.

findings.finding: The confidence reads 'High, if the caveats below aren't material' over a caveat that the page itself shows is plausibly material. The pick's computed interval, 96.2–98.1%, crosses the gate, and a fresh run reads it below 38.6% of the time. The best-of-eighteen caveat pushes the same way. Fix it one of two ways. Option one: scope the High to what holds, namely that the pick is the cheapest configuration passing on point estimates as declared, and only the Brisk-S fallback is close. Then say plainly that the High does not cover whether the pick truly clears 97%, and that the fresh read in Next settles it. Option two: make the form low.

Watch and Next cite 111,255 cases to settle the pick 'four times in five', but claim settle's table prints only 38,350 (one-sided, half of runs) and 54,451 (two-sided). 111,255 is the two-sided, four-in-five size (settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.cases_needed_two_sided_80). Add that column, or the 80% sizes, to the settle table and say which one the decision uses, so the reader can find Watch's figure in the evidence.

The block gives prices per point but not the gains they divide by: +0.8 points from the pick to the high-reasoning fallback, and +0.7 from there to Atlas-M · reasoning high · 1 retry. Its caption also says neither gain carries an interval, yet claim multihop prints -0.4 to +2.1 for the first gain. Add the gains and the monthly cost gaps ($1,324 and $11,376) to the table. Then say the first gain's unpaired interval crosses zero, so $1,595.18 a month per point has no upper bound that the data support.

The claim rests on the pick's 95.6% on multi-hop, which the block doesn't draw: it shows only the fallback-minus-pick differences. Add the pick's own task rates, or a column for them. Also soften 'gains most' (+1.7). The task rows carry no interval, and the overall +0.8 has an interval of -0.4 to +2.1, so the task ordering is descriptive, not established.

The lower bound on the high-reasoning retry effect prints as '+0.03535'. Round it like the others (+0.04, or +0.0). The claim's $0.014 extra cost per 1,000 calls is not in the block; either add the two arms' costs or drop the figure from the sentence.

Claim pick and the decision's 'Why not the others' rank models by cost: the cheapest passing Atlas-M is 5.5 times the pick's cost. No provider is named for any arm. The routing caveat covers this up top, but the claim itself should say the costs are as routed in this run, with the provider not recorded, so the cross-model ratio is not read as a property of the models.

The third next step reruns the tuned pick 'on the same 1,200 cases' after teaching it on those cases' failures. A pass there wouldn't show it clears the gate with room on new traffic. Name fresh or held-out cases, sized against the settle figures.
